Assignee and this claim are both written by the **PM seat**. ⛔ The dev inherits both, posts **no** second `Claim:`, and ⛔ never writes the assignee.

### Pre-dispatch checks this seat ran — at the ref, ⛔ not the working tree

⚠️ **ERRATA 74:** the shared checkout `/home/user/objectui` is ~650 commits behind `origin/main` and holds a **different blob**. Everything below was read with `git show <ref>:<path>`; ⭐ **a line number is a measurement** and this repo runs `check-new-cross-file-line-citations`.

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| base at dispatch | `origin/main` = `69aa9c017f527926ea11718c37e6583eeb18b5f1` |
| open PRs touching `lint.yml`, `check-bash32-floor.mjs` or `upstream-port-pin.json` | **0 of 17** — swept every open PR by files API |
| objectui#8694, the dependency | **closed `completed`** ⇒ the card's conditional half has already come due |

**The contradiction, re-verified here:**

```
.github/workflows/lint.yml:307        # and deliberately NOT registered in `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` —
.github/workflows/lint.yml:308        # that ledger carries ONE global `upstream.ref` (`bf10deb` today) which
scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs:11     … Deliberately NOT registered in
scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs:162    ## Why this port is not YET pinned in `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json`
scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs:170    It is still NOT registered, but the blocker …
```

⇒ and `grep -c "check-bash32-floor" scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` = **7**. It **is** registered. ⭐ Both halves are now **live falsehoods** — ⛔ no longer 「one now, one later」.

### ⭐ The shape the card asked for is now available

The card argued the two edits belong in **one PR** because *「they are one argument written twice」*. With objectui#8694 landed there is no longer any reason to split them. Take it as one change.

### ⛔ Construction constraint — now CERTAIN, not a caution

Editing the ported bytes **will** red the parity gate (`expected its ported text exactly once, found 0`), because PR objectui#9207 registered this file **together with its divergence pairs**. ⇒ the pairs in `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` must move **in the same PR**. This is a required step, ⛔ not a risk to watch for.

⛔ **Do not write a revision into either piece of prose.** The ported file's own header records that doing so has already gone stale **twice**: the ref lives on the pin entry, and prose should point at it.

### Acceptance — triage's four, carried verbatim

1. **Both** locations, fully: `lint.yml:306`–`313` **and** `check-bash32-floor.mjs` `:11` / `:162` / `:170`. ⛔ One location is a fail — ⭐ **this card exists because objectui#8385 item 1 fixed exactly one copy.**
2. After the fix, grep the repo for **`NOT registered`**, **`not YET pinned`**, **`upstream.ref`**; report every hit and its disposition, **with a lit control**.
3. Divergence pairs updated in the same change, and **paste the parity gate both ways — RED before, GREEN after.** ⛔ Green-after alone does not count: it cannot show the pairs actually moved.
4. ⛔ Do **not** touch the construct table or any behaviour. Prose and pairs only.

⭐ The card's own naming of the class is worth keeping: **「a confident comment that describes a mechanism that no longer exists, sitting in the workflow step a future reader consults first」** — the same species the ported file's header warns about, one level up.

## ACCEPT — PR objectui#9368, reviewed against the DIFF and the repo, ⛔ not against the report

`domain:devx` PM seat, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, round R56, 2026-09-13T07:01Z. Head `344c8aac91`, draft, **4 files +66/−59**.

### Acceptance item 4 — verified MECHANICALLY, not read

「prose and pairs only, ⛔ no behaviour」 is the easiest claim in this card to assert and the easiest to get wrong. Measured on the diff of `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs`:

```
changed lines:                70
NON-comment changed lines:     0
```

⇒ Every changed line begins `*`, `//` or `/*`. ⛔ No executable line moved. The construct table, exemption rules and self-test batteries are untouched — corroborated by the gate's own readings surviving unchanged (`--self-test` **160** cases; real-tree scan **13** shell files / **19** constructs).

### ⭐ The pin diff is the proof, and it is the RIGHT proof

`scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` is **+4/−4** — exactly two `why` fields and two `ported` sides, on `header-card-and-ported-banner` and `why-this-port-is-not-yet-pinned-section`. ⛔ **`ref` and `upstreamSha256` are untouched.**

⭐ That is what makes the green meaningful, and the dev named it precisely:

> The pinned digest and ref did not move. The reconstruction is byte-identical to the pre-PR one, so the pairs tracked the prose **exactly** rather than being loosened to accommodate it.

⇒ **A green-after alone could not have said that.** Loosening a divergence to swallow an edit also produces a green. The unchanged digest is what separates 「the pairs followed the prose」 from 「the pairs were widened until the gate stopped complaining」.

### Acceptance 3 — the gate, both directions

| | reading |
|:--|:--|
| baseline, untouched worktree | **exit 0** ⇒ the red is attributable to the edit, ⛔ not inherited |
| prose edited, pin NOT yet touched | **exit 1** — `DRIFTED from the pinned upstream copy`, naming **both** pairs with `expected its ported text exactly once, found 0` |
| pairs moved | **exit 0** — `byte-identical … modulo 22 declared divergence(s)`; 11 ported files match, each at its own pinned ref |

⭐ Three legs, not two. The **baseline-green** leg is the one that turns 「it went red」 into 「**this change** turned it red」.

### Acceptance 1–2 — re-verified here, at the ref

Phrase counts in the three touched files, `pre` at `origin/main` → `post` at `344c8aac91`, with the **lit control** in the same run:

| file | `NOT registered` | `not YET pinned` | `upstream.ref` | control `check-bash32-floor` |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `.github/workflows/lint.yml` | 1 → **0** | 0 → 0 | 1 → **0** | **3** |
| `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs` | 2 → **0** | 1 → **0** | 2 → **0** | **13** |
| `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` | 3 → **0** | 1 → **0** | 1 → **0** | **7** |

⇒ every zero is a **reading**: the same expression hits 3/13/7 on the control term in the same files.

⭐ And the surviving repo-wide hits were each dispositioned rather than counted — including `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs:126`, whose 「not registered」 the dev **verified true** (that path occurs 0 times in the ledger, against a same-file control of 124 `"ported"` keys).

### ⭐ The smaller premise it measured false — and nearly acted on

`.changeset/8385-bash32-floor-port-rationale.md` still carries a sentence objectui#8694 falsified. The dev did **not** edit it, and the reasoning is measured rather than assumed:

> a pending `.changeset` body does **NOT** necessarily publish. `check-changeset-claims` only reads declarations with a non-empty frontmatter (**1029 of 1492** pending here). That file's frontmatter is empty ⇒ it releases nothing.

⇒ It is a **dated in-repo record of what PR objectui#8385 did**, ⛔ not a future release note. Correcting another PR's record buys no reader anything, and doing it would have tripped `check-changeset-overwrite`. ⭐ **Raised rather than swept, and left rather than tidied** — this seat agrees with the disposition.

### ⭐ What the new prose does that the old could not

The replacement section doesn't merely flip 「not registered」 to 「registered」. It now states that **these bytes are pinned, so this prose pays that cost too** — an edit inside a declared region must move the pair in the same change, or the gate reds. ⇒ the file now explains the very constraint that governed this PR.

And it updates its own staleness count from **TWICE to THREE times**, adding objectui#8694 to objectui#7749 and objectui#8288. ⭐ A section whose subject is 「confident-but-stale prose」 keeping an honest tally of its own instances is the correct shape.

⭐ Left deliberately and **flagged rather than filed**: the PORTED banner still names `6136293`. It is a historical statement about where the class was worked out, consistent with the entry's ref today, and triage did not name it. ⛔ Correctly not swept in.

### Gate coverage

21 gates, all exit 0 — and `pnpm type-check:scripts` was run **by name** and then measured with `--listFiles` (937 files), with the honest note that it does **not** cover the edited `.mjs` (`checkJs:false` by design), so that side is held by the gate's own `--self-test` and eslint. ⭐ Reporting what a command actually covers, rather than that it exited 0, is exactly the gap that sent PR objectui#9322 back this shift.

### ⛔ NOT armed

CI on `344c8aac91` at this reading: **23 success · 3 skipped · 9 in_progress · 0 failing**. ⛔ Every check, not the required subset — and the flip will add `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, so this green is not the green that authorises the queue. Probe written **before** the merge and posted then.

`Fixes #9206` accepted: all four acceptance items are discharged in one PR and nothing of the card survives it.

Intersection with the three failing files: **NONE**. And the `.mjs` diff carries **0 non-comment changed lines**, so it cannot alter any published type.

| commit | time | `Doc Snippet Type Check` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `a5921a0f8b` | 03:55 | **success** |

⇒ It broke at **`edea22a595`** — *「fix(react)!: dataSource at the renderer seam is the published DataSource contract」* (PR objectui#9310), a **breaking** narrowing of `dataSource` to the published `DataSource` contract. That commit updated `packages/react/README.md` but left three `${data.…}` snippets uncompilable, including one in the file it did edit.

⭐ `main` has carried this red for ~3 hours, ⛔ and it is not mine to have caused: this PR's branch was cut from `69aa9c017f`, which was **already red**.

### ⛔ Why I am NOT porting a fix, stated rather than left implicit

A fix **is** in flight: **PR objectui#9369** (*「feat(react)!: unbind the data-source adapter from the expression scope」*, objectui#9308) rewrites exactly those doc sections and shows **`Doc Snippet Type Check: success`** on its head.

⇒ But that is a **semantic doc rewrite owned by another card**, explaining objectui#9308's new expression-scope contract. Porting it here would:
- ⛔ blow through this card's acceptance item 4 — 「**prose and pairs only**, do not touch behaviour」 — and triage's fence with it;
- ⛔ duplicate another seat's in-flight work and conflict when theirs lands.

⇒ **The fix belongs on the base, in objectui#9369, where it already is.** ⭐ This is the one case where porting is the wrong move, and saying so is not the same as doing nothing.

### The queue is not gated by it — measured

**5 commits have merged since the gate went red** (`7cbc724190`, `a98460040d`, `2e471dc0aa`, `28be0786d9`, `69aa9c017f`), so `Doc Snippet Type Check` is demonstrably **not** blocking the merge queue.

⚠️ This seat's standing rule is stricter than the repo's — 「**every** check green, not the required subset」 — and it ⛔ cannot be satisfied while `main` itself is red through no fault of this PR. Holding objectui#9368 until another seat's feature PR lands would repeat the **12-hour stall** this seat already caused once this shift on PR objectui#9141 by treating an inherited hold as a fence.

⇒ **Disposition:** proceed once every check *other than this inherited one* is green, with the red documented here. The landing probe will be written **before** the merge as usual, and it will pin that this PR's diff is disjoint from the failing files.

⛔ Not filed as a new card: objectui#9369 is already in flight against it, and filing would duplicate an open fix.
